name: Neumorphism / Soft UI
era: 2019-2021 (peak in early 2020), a quotation style ever since
origin: The trigger was a Dribbble shot by Alexander Plyuto in late 2019: a banking app concept in which controls no longer sit on the surface but appear pressed out of it. Jason Kelly and Michal Malewicz coined the name shortly after, a portmanteau of 'neo' and 'skeuomorphism'. The style was the backlash against six years of flat design and its affordance problem: after iOS 7 nobody knew what was clickable any more, and neumorphism gave buttons a physical shape again -- without the leather and wood textures of old skeuomorphism. Technically it was trivial, because two box-shadow values on an identical base color are enough; that cheapness is exactly what made it go viral.
idea: Element and background carry exactly the same color; shape comes solely from a light shadow at the top left and a dark one at the bottom right, as if the surface were extruded out of soft plastic or pressed into it.
markers: Element fill == background color, canonically #E0E5EC -- no surface value of its own
Double shadow: 9px 9px 18px #A3B1C6 and -9px -9px 18px #FFFFFF, light source fixed at the top left
Edge contrast element/background only 1.3-1.7:1 -- measurably below the WCAG threshold of 3:1
Radius 20-34px on surfaces and cards, 999px on fields and pills
Not a single border value in the entire UI
Pressed state as a pure inversion into inset shadows, no color change
Recessed elements (search field, slots, grooves) via inset instead of a fill color
Exactly one elevation level -- layers stacked above or below one another cannot be rendered

params.radius: 20-34px on surfaces and cards, 999px on pills and input fields
params.depth: Pseudo-relief from two opposing shadows on the same base color; extruded (outset) vs. pressed in (inset), nothing in between
params.color: Monochrome: a single light blue-gray base, everything else is shadow gradations of the same color; at most one desaturated accent for numbers and the primary action
params.type: Soft, rounded grotesque at 600-800, mid-gray instead of black, with a letterpress text shadow
params.motion: Only the shadow switch: box-shadow 200-220ms ease from outset to inset on press, no movement of the geometry
params.texture: none -- the surface is deliberately flawless and smooth

examples.name: Alexander Plyuto, 'Skeuomorph Mobile Banking' (Dribbble, Dec. 2019)
examples.what: The originating shot: credit card, circular buttons and sliders all in #E0E5EC, shape coming only from the double shadow; icons as thin lines, not a single border

examples.name: neumorphism.io (Adrian Bece)
examples.what: A generator that exposes exactly the four parameters of the style: distance, blur, intensity, inset/outset -- effectively the specification of the look

examples.name: macOS Big Sur (2020)
examples.what: Softly extruded, slightly plastic icon shapes on light gray chrome -- the most mass-market form of soft extrusion, though only on icons, never on surfaces, and without the double-shadow formula

examples.name: Michal Malewicz, 'Neumorphism in user interfaces' (2019/2020)
examples.what: The article in whose comments the name was born -- and which was also the first to name the contrast problem

examples.name: Samsung One UI (from 2019)
examples.what: Rounded, very low-contrast containers on a light gray ground -- a heavily toned-down product variant that adopts the soft feel without committing to the double shadow

strengths: Unmistakable within 200 ms -- no other style looks like this
Very calm and tactile; reads like a device, not like a document
Technically trivial: two box-shadow values, no assets, no images, no font license
The pressed state is as visually unambiguous as on a real key
risks: Only one elevation level is possible -- modals, popovers, dropdowns or toasts have no representable place in the system
No light/dark switch without a complete redesign: the double-shadow logic breaks down on a dark ground and needs different curves
On small displays, at low brightness or in compressed screenshots the relief disappears entirely
Disabled, pressed and normal states are barely distinguishable once there are three forms
Tips over into 'cheap plastic toy' as soon as the blur gets too large or the base color too saturated
a11y: The style is by construction not WCAG-compliant: the load-bearing edge between control and background reaches 1.27:1 (light edge) to 1.72:1 (dark edge) in this demo, where WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 requires at least 3:1 for control boundaries. Body text can be salvaged (#4C5C73 on #E0E5EC = 5.38:1, AA passed), secondary information such as timestamps falls below at 2.44:1, and the accent tone sits just under the threshold at 2.98:1. A focus ring has to be retrofitted as a hard, style-breaking outline, because a neumorphic ring will never meet the contrast requirements -- this demo does exactly that on :focus-visible.
longevity: Hard-dated to 2020: anyone who sees the look today immediately reads 'Dribbble trend from the pandemic years'. It has no institutional foothold that would let it survive as a niche the way skeuomorphism does in pro audio.

platforms.web: Trivial in CSS, but the double shadows cost real paint time on long lists and the style does not scale beyond a single elevation level.
platforms.mobile: Practically unusable on Android and iOS: in bright ambient light and on OLED panels with aggressive contrast management the relief disappears, and both platforms mandate a dark mode the style does not have.
platforms.desktop: Technically unproblematic in Tauri, but desktop UIs need menus, popovers and dialogs -- exactly the layers neumorphism cannot render.

verdict: As the basis of a brand of your own: a clear no. Not because it is ugly, but because it structurally violates three of the client's requirements: it has no dark theme, no second elevation level and no WCAG-compliant control edge -- and since the European Accessibility Act the last of those is no longer a matter of taste. For a brand spanning web, Tauri and Compose that means three separate redesigns instead of one token set. What can be carried over is exactly one detail: the inset inversion as an active state on a single component (toggle, segmented control) -- a cheap, tactile carrier of recognizability that works without the rest of the style.
tip: Never pick a blur larger than the distance (9px/18px, not 9px/40px) and keep the base color at roughly 88-92% lightness with a slight blue cast -- pure gray looks dead, saturated gray looks like a toy. And: the only way to make the style usable is a second, style-breaking signal channel per state (color, icon or text), because the relief alone does not carry the state.

finder.signature: Not a single border value in the whole UI; the pressed state is a plain inversion of the two shadows.
